title: What is the BCG interview process, and how should you prepare?
description: BCG's hiring steps explained: application, online assessments such as the Casey chatbot case, the skill, case and team interviews, and how to prepare.
hook: BCG describes its interviews as a two-way conversation: you are assessing them as much as they are assessing you. That is a helpful way to walk in. Here is how the process usually works and how to get ready for each part.
body:
The steps

  1. Application through BCG's careers site, with your CV and, depending on office, a cover letter and transcripts.
  2. Online assessment, which varies by office. Many candidates take the BCG Online Case, delivered by a chatbot called Casey: one business case answered through a chat interface, followed by a short recorded video recommendation.
  3. Interviews. BCG's own careers site describes a skill interview (your experience, skills and motivation), a case interview and a team interview.
  4. Offer. Prep guides commonly report four to eight weeks from application to decision.

The case: usually candidate-led

In live interviews, BCG cases are usually candidate-led: you are expected to structure, ask for data and drive. Practise proposing your next step after every answer. The Casey chatbot is the exception: the chatbot leads, so it feels interviewer-led.

What BCG looks for

BCG's careers pages talk about problem solving, creative thinking, a collaborative mindset and drive. Show creativity in your brainstorms, and be a good colleague in the interview: listen, build on hints and stay curious.

How to prepare

  • Use BCG's case interview preparation page and its practice material.
  • Practise candidate-led cases with a partner, including at least one where you get stuck and must recover.
  • For Casey, practise maths and chart questions under time pressure, and a one-minute spoken recommendation.
  • Prepare clear answers on why consulting and why BCG.

Sources

  • BCG: Interview process
  • BCG: Case interview preparation
  • Hacking the Case Interview: BCG hiring process
  • Hacking the Case Interview: BCG Online Case

Checked November 2026. Processes change by office and year, so always confirm with the firm's own careers page and your recruiter.

Demonstrate a decision, not just a framework

For practice, consider a retailer deciding whether to launch a lower-priced private-label line. Start by clarifying whether the objective is profit, market share, customer retention or a combination. Then investigate demand and likely cannibalisation, unit economics, retailer capacity, competitor reaction and execution risks. Say where you would begin: "I'd first estimate incremental contribution after sales lost from our existing products."

Suppose the new line earns £2 per item and is forecast to sell 500,000 items, but 200,000 sales replace an existing product that contributes £3 per item. The incremental annual contribution is £400,000, not £1 million: 500,000 × £2 minus 200,000 × £3. That single calculation shows why commercial judgement matters alongside structure.

Practise explaining the calculation without reading from notes, then present a recommendation with one uncertainty that could reverse it. Confirm whether your particular office is using a live, online, group or written assessment. A third-party guide may accurately describe someone's experience without describing yours.
